title: fix(metadata-protocol)!: the metadata save door never sets, changes or removes an item's lock: a body's `_lock*` family is kept from the stored row, echoed, or refused
body:
Fixes #23119
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

## What changes

The metadata save door (`PUT /api/v1/meta/{type}/{name}`, and every write that reaches `saveMetaItem`'s author arm) used to store a body's `_lock*` family (`_lock`, `_lockReason`, `_lockDocsUrl`, `_lockSource`) verbatim. A hand-written or echoed `_lock: 'full'` then bound an environment item for good: the next save and the delete each answered `403 ITEM_LOCKED`, and no door unlocks it. The reverse also held: an author save that sent no `_lock*` key dropped a lock a server face had stamped on the row.

Per the binding triage direction (6135754247), the author arm now keeps the lock family the row it writes already stores, beside `protectionBlockRefusal` and in its refusal family:

| body sends | outcome |
|---|---|
| no `_lock*` key | saved; the row keeps its stored family (not a removal) |
| a family equal to one a read of this item serves | accepted and ignored (the row keeps its stored family) |
| anything else: an add, a change (state or prose), a removal (`_lock: 'none'`, a partial echo), a family copied from another item | `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, nothing written |

- The refusal names every `_lock*` key sent and ADR-0010's door ("declare `protection` on it in a code package's source, where the package loader translates it into the item's lock (ADR-0010 Phase 4.3)"); `issues[]` carries each key as a path. Not a silent strip. On an item that serves no lock, a family that binds nothing (a lone prose key, or `_lock: none`) is described as adding lock keys rather than setting a lock.
- Server-stated faces (`source`, `writeFace: 'package-duplicate'`) keep stamping as before. The unmanaged import's strip (`stripUnmanagedImportLock`) is untouched.
- A `_lock*` value the type's own declaration refuses (`_lock: 'locked'`, a non-string reason) is handed to the parse untouched and still answers `422 INVALID_METADATA`, so the unmanaged import's documented refusal of such an item (pinned in `package-unmanaged-install.test.ts`) does not move.
- No stored lock is unbound.

`item-lock.ts`: the docblock sentence that called a stored row lock "an administrator's stored lock" now reads it as amended in 6135754247 (one the runtime stamped, never one an author wrote). Prose only: the resolver, the `overlay` layer and the layer order are untouched. `shared/protection.zod.ts` is not edited: its guidance ("never authored") is true without naming the save door, and becomes more true with this change.

## What the echo is compared against, and why

Two families count as "what the read served for that item":

1. **The item's resolved lock at the save's address**: the one item-lock resolution's answer, `resolveItemLock` over every shipping package's artifact (`artifactLockLayerAt`) and the strictest stored row in scope (`overlayLockLayerAt`, `otherSpelling: true`, exactly as the reads pass it), written as a family by `withItemLockFamily`. This is what `getMetaItem`'s `item`, the layered read's `effective` and the list serve, i.e. what `servedLockState` reports and what Studio and AI Studio echo.
2. **The family stored on the row this save writes** (the repository's write-address resolution, `headAt`, at the save's state, package and bundle member; a first draft reads the active row it overlays). This is what the draft read, the `previewDrafts` read and the layered read's `overlay` layer serve verbatim. Accepting it changes nothing, since it is the family carried forward anyway. It is load-bearing for a real producer: the permission-set data door merges its patch into `getMetaItemLayered().overlay` and saves into that row, and a row storing `_lock: 'none'` serves an empty resolved family.

A new item has no row and serves no lock, so any family on it is an add. A first overlay of a packaged item echoes the artifact's family: accepted, the new row stores none, and the package's lock still binds through the artifact layer. The layered read's raw `code` layer is deliberately not an echo source (see Acceptance notes).

## Measured faces that reach the author arm

The arm is `request.source === undefined && request.writeFace !== 'package-duplicate'`. Measured on `f931e765b7` (base) with a protocol probe saving `{ _lock: 'no-delete' }` on each face (all stored it verbatim before; after, every author face answers `400`, both server faces still stamp):

| face | who | body carries `_lock*`? | treatment |
|---|---|---|---|
| `meta-envelope` | REST `PUT` | author's | judged |
| `meta-dispatch` | runtime dispatcher | author's | judged |
| no face | in-process doors: flow save and clone, permission-set clone, permission-set data door and backfill, position write-through and backfill, the package publish's app flip | the clones drop `_lock*`; the data door merges into the stored overlay body; the app flip re-saves the list's served body | judged (echoes pass) |
| `external-import` | service-datasource "Import as Object" | never: the body is server-built from introspection plus name and label (code read of `importObject`) | carry-forward only |
| `package-unmanaged-import` | `importUnmanagedPackage` | never a well-formed one: `stripUnmanagedImportLock` drops it, and the import writes only names no row held | carry-forward only (no row, so no family) |

No face that reaches the arm stamps a lock in fact, so the direction's shape holds; no `needs_decision`. A type with no schema (`external_catalog`: the only registry type whose schema does not declare `_lock`) is judged too, because no parse refuses the key there and the `_lock` gate reads it from any stored body.

## Readings, before and after

Protocol door (the `saveMetaItem` / `getMetaItem` / `deleteMetaItem` the REST `PUT` / `GET` / `DELETE` forward to), stub engine with real rows. A showcase boot was not re-run (see Narrowings).

| reading | base `f931e765b7` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `PUT app/probe_rawlock_app` with `_lock: 'full', _lockReason: 'raw'` | `200`, row stores the family | `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, no row |
| `GET` after it | `lock: 'full'`, `editable: false`, `deletable: false` | item absent; the same body without the family saves and reads `lock: 'none'`, editable, deletable |
| second `PUT` / `DELETE` | `403 ITEM_LOCKED` / `403 ITEM_LOCKED` | `200` / `200` |
| a server-stamped `no-delete`, then an author save with no family | lock dropped: read `lock: 'none'`, `DELETE` `200` | lock kept: read `lock: 'no-delete'`, `DELETE` `403 ITEM_LOCKED` |
| echo of a packaged `no-delete` on its first overlay | the overlay row stores the package's family | `200`, the overlay row stores none, the item still reads `no-delete` |

## Tests

At `6bbc5475cc` unless stated.

- New `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.save-door-lock-family.test.ts`: 25 tests, pass. On both author faces: the card's probe; the add (every lock state and a lone prose key), the change (state, reason, docs URL) and the removal (`none`, a partial echo) each refused with the envelope (`code` + `status` via `resolveThrownHttpError`) and the `issues[]` paths; draft add refused; echo accepted for a server-stamped row, for a packaged item's first overlay, in draft mode (first draft and the draft read's own echo, then publish keeps the lock), and on a clone of an unlocked item, while a clone carrying another item's lock is refused. Plus: both server faces stamp and the stamp survives author saves; `full` still answers `403 ITEM_LOCKED` first; CONTROL body without a family; CONTROL malformed values stay `422 INVALID_METADATA`; an in-process door; `external_catalog`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` (whole package, run at `2ed18c717c`, implementation unchanged since): 230 files passed, 1 failed (`protocol.package-publish-audit-rows.test.ts`, 5 tests: its fixtures seeded a stored lock through the author face, the door this card closes). Fixture moved onto the server face (`source: 'migrate-stored'`) in `063ca29be4`; that file plus the new one re-run: 2 files, 43 tests pass.
- Resolver and neighbour pins re-run, files untouched: `protocol.lock-one-resolution.test.ts` (#21738's resolver pin), `protocol.save-door-protection.test.ts`, `package-unmanaged-install.test.ts`, `protocol.lock-door-read-agree.test.ts`: 4 files, 24129 tests pass.
- `packages/objectql`: the 53 test files that mention `saveMetaItem` or `_lock` (against a rebuilt `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` dist, 5 hits of the new method in `dist/index.js`): 53 files, 740 tests pass. `protocol-derived-provenance-doors.test.ts` pinned the verbatim store ("does NOT touch the _lock* family"); it now pins the same intent under the new rule: a stored family is kept while the three derived keys go, and an authored family is refused with nothing written.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol run typecheck` exit 0 (`--listFiles` includes both edited test files); `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql run typecheck` exit 0 (tsc plus `check:test-typecheck`, debt held).

## Ablation (one-time, not kept)

`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced the arm's `request.item = await this.authoredLockFamily({` with a no-op that returns the body (the verbatim store), on the committed tree, with a trap restore. On disk: anchor 1 to 0, marker 0 to 1, blob `5ce2896165` to `8faf50ed0d`. The subject resolves through `./protocol.js` (source, no `dist/` involved).

- Ablated: 18 failed, 7 passed of 25. Red: every add, change and removal pin, the draft add, the clone-refused half, the in-process door, `external_catalog`, both server-stamp carry-forward pins (the verbatim store drops the stamped lock), and the packaged first-overlay echo pin (the verbatim store copies the package's family into the row, so its "stores none" assertion goes red: the "ignored" half). Green: the stored-row echo (both faces), the draft echo (both faces), `full` answering `ITEM_LOCKED`, and both CONTROLs.
- Restored: blob equals the HEAD blob `5ce2896165`, `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Gates

The dispatch's 80-command lead list plus the families derived on this diff (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`, 75 families; union 98 commands), each run sequentially with its exit captured before any pipe: 95 exit 0, including `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main` ("1 declared-breaking changeset(s), each carrying an ADR-0087 disposition"), `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-empty-changeset`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:error-status-conformance`, `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary`, `check:durability-log-level`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:type-check-debt`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`.

- `check:engine-double-contract` was red (exit 1) until the new test's pinned doubles were recorded (`--write`: 3 rows added, 0 lost) in `6bbc5475cc`; re-run exit 0.
- NOT MEASURED: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:lean-entry-closure`, reason: both exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET), they load built entry points for packages this worktree did not build. CI runs both.
- `dispatch-gates --ran` reconciliation: 75 derived families accounted for, 75 run.
- Lint: `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 5 touched TypeScript files at `6bbc5475cc`: 5 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. Population: `eslint.config.mjs` lints `**/*.ts` minus its `NEVER_LINTED` list, and none of the 5 is ignored (no "file ignored" warning). Invariance: the config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, stated at its own `:327`), so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.

## Narrowings (declared)

- After about an hour of `os-verify-lock` queue timeouts behind another seat's full builds and dogfood batteries, the light targeted runs above (the two-file, four-file and 53-file vitest runs, the ablation and the two typechecks) ran outside the lock with `--maxWorkers=2`. The closure build and the first full package run went through the lock.
- No showcase boot: the readings are taken at the protocol door the REST routes forward to. `packages/qa/dogfood` (`install-local-unmanaged-mode.dogfood.test.ts` saves each copied item's served body back) was not run locally: it needs the full build, and it rides main's full battery. Its copied bodies carry no `_lock*` key, so they pass as no-family saves.

## Changeset

`.changeset/23119-save-door-lock-envelope.md`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: minor`, `**BREAKING**`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Level: the WHICH LEVEL rule in `pr-automation.yml` grades a widening `minor` and a fix that changes no public surface `patch`; this narrows a published accept set, which is a breaking change, and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` states that during the launch window a breaking change ships `minor` (the grade #23096's entry took for the same door). The arm: `clause2-line.mjs` defines `no (narrowing)` as "NOT a widening, but breaking", which is this diff. No `@objectstack/spec` entry: its prose is not changed. The changeset supersedes one sentence of the pending `23096-save-door-protection` entry, its "A body without `protection` saves as before": that now holds only for a body that also sends no `_lock*` key or sends back exactly the `_lock*` family a read of that item serves. No sentence of a pending `15213-*` entry becomes false.

## Acceptance notes

- **Deviations from the file surface.** The rule needs helpers: `LOCK_FAMILY_KEYS` (derived from `MetadataProtectionFields`, so this file adds no hand-kept list beside the one `item-lock.ts` already keeps), `lockFamilyOf`, `sameLockFamily`, `withLockFamily` and `authoredLockFamilyRefusal` sit beside `protectionBlockRefusal`, and the private `authoredLockFamily` sits just above `saveMetaItem`; the arm itself gains one call. Outside `protocol.ts`, three existing files had to move with the behaviour: the objectql provenance-door pin and the publish-audit fixtures (both relied on the author face storing a lock), and `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` (the new test's doubles).
- **Cost.** Every author-arm save makes one more indexed `sys_metadata` head read (the target row, plus the active row for a first draft), with no `try`/`catch`: a stored lock that cannot be read fails the save rather than being written away. A body that carries a `_lock*` family not equal to the stored one adds the served-lock read (artifact lookup plus the rows in scope).
- **Boundary: the layered `code` layer is not an echo source.** For a package that declares `protection.lock: 'none'`, that raw layer carries `_lock: 'none'` while every resolved read serves no family; a body copied from it is refused, loudly, with a one-step remedy (remove the keys).
- **A malformed `_lock*` value** gets the parse's `422` first and this door's `400` only once it is well-formed. Accepted to keep the unmanaged import's refusal unchanged.
- **Existing state is untouched.** A row (or a pending draft) that already stores an author-written lock keeps it, and publishing such a draft still promotes it: unbinding is the maintainer's (triage 6135754247), and a reported stuck item is the ADR-0010 §3.8 card.
